author: BBC News
description:
President Trump has announced that he is "immediately" banning CNN, Politico and MS Now from the White House, the latest twist in his fraught relationship with the media.

In a post on Truth Social on Friday, Trump said that the outlets "constantly write or report fiction or lies" about his administration, although he provided no examples.

Trump later called it a "very simple ban", but did not explain how it would work. It is unclear whether employees of those outlets would be prevented from entering the White House grounds.

CNN swiftly slammed the move as an "illegal assault" on American media freedoms. The move by Trump is likely to be met with legal challenges.

In a statement, the network called a potential ban illegal and said it "stands fully behind our White House team and their fair and accurate reporting."

title: US President Donald Trump bans CNN and Politico from White House | BBC News

As the midterm elections in America approach, the economy is one of the deciding factors for how people will vote.

Before his second term started, President Trump promised to tackle the so-called affordability crisis. But since then, the war in Iran has led to soaring gas prices and a range of tariffs have made some goods more expensive.

How do global events impact people’s finances and in turn how they vote in elections? The talk show host and financial expert Dave Ramsey joins us to discuss.

author: BBC News
description:
Has the AI industry finally recognised the dangers of the technology it is building?

A researcher leaves one of the world's leading AI companies with a warning that the race to build ever more powerful systems could end in human extinction. Days later, the chief executive of the same company calls for the industry to slow down.

In this episode AI Decoded examines the growing debate over AI safety, regulation and control. From fears that advanced systems could outpace human understanding to concerns over cyberattacks, biological threats and the challenge of containing increasingly powerful models, the programme asks whether the world's AI companies are moving too fast, and whether anyone can agree on how to slow down.

Our panel also explores AI "kill switches", international oversight, the role of governments, and whether rivalry between the United States and China makes meaningful cooperation impossible.

description:
Are we in for a winter of financial hope or pain?  

The Bank of England has held interest rates at 3.75% in a move which might come as some relief for mortgage holders. However the Bank’s governor has warned about high energy costs coming down the line.   

The move comes in contrast to the US Federal Reserve increased interest rates for the first time in more than three years. So what does this say about the UK economy? And, for the impact on the cost of living in Winter?  Adam, Chris and Faisal are joined by Stephanie Flanders, head of Economics and Government at Bloomberg.

description:
Thirty-seven people accused of illegal mining in north-central Nigeria have died in custody, local officials said.
 
The Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps blamed on an apparent disease outbreak.
 
However, an intelligence report shared with the AFP news agency suggested the group died because of overcrowding and poor ventilation inside the detention facility in Niger state.
 
Police have set up an investigation into the deaths.

description:
Police in the West Midlands say drones are playing a “key role” in helping prevent trouble outside of stadiums as part of a £2m pilot.
 
The Premier League described the pilot as "really positive" in tackling potential incidents as they occur, by deploying officers where they are needed as footage is fed into a control room in real time.
 
The drones are only deployed before and after matches to ensure fans' safety, West Midlands Police says.
